gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much continuous power each battery's own BMS allows (BMS amps × nominal volts). That figure is the largest inverter load the battery can carry. For 12V 100Ah packs it is 1,280 W with Redodo's 100 A BMS and 1,920 W with Vatrer's 150 A BMS, at almost the same price per Wh ($0.19–0.21).
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no results or catalog cards, so there were no rival pages to read. Its own answer lists what a BMS protects against and gives nominal voltages for 4S/8S/16S packs. It names no product and gives no current rating, continuous wattage, Wh per lb, $ per Wh or cost per lifetime kWh. Every derived figure below is new against that answer. It decides the pick only for buyers running a large inverter, because $ per Wh is close to tied across the 12V 100Ah options.
decides: For a 12V buyer running an inverter above about 1,280 W DC, the Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24 (150 A BMS, 1,920 W) is the right 100Ah pick at the same $259.99 as Redodo's Group 24 Bluetooth (100 A BMS, 1,280 W). Below 1,280 W, Redodo wins on weight and price: the Ultra-Mini gives 64.6 Wh/lb and the Low-Temp Trolling model costs $0.183/Wh. For 48V home storage, the Sun Gold Power SG48100P has the lowest cost per lifetime kWh ($0.027) because its rated cycle count is the highest (≥7,000).
